articles.title: Ranking WWE and AEW's Most Underrated Stars of 2026
articles.summary: We're closing in on the end of the year, and that means people are going to start looking back at 2026 in different ways.
articles.body:
We're closing in on the end of the year, and that means people are going to start looking back at 2026 in different ways.

This past year was an interesting time for pro wrestling. While WWE has been in the news for a lot of reasons, both good and bad, AEW spent most of the year trying to highlight a lot of newer faces in the company.

With so many men and women employed between the two companies, it's never going to be possible for every single person who deserves a push to get one, and that often leads to a lot of people not getting the proper attention.

Whether they are underrated by the fans, management, or in some other way, a lot of people across both companies have been very valuable and deserve more attention in 2027.

This list will be ranked by how underrated someone is in relation to their booking, not against each other.

Ricochet came into AEW, quickly turned heel, formed a faction with Bishop Kaun and Toa Liona, and he has been a regular fixture ever since.

Whether Tony Khan needs to have someone win a title, put someone else over, play a villain, or just go out and have a fantastic match, Ricochet is the man for the job.

He has been nothing short of incredible in the ring against a variety of AEW stars, and his heel run has been so entertaining that it makes you wonder why WWE never allowed him to give it a shot.

The only thing holding Ricochet back is available space at the top of the card. He is part of one of the most stacked rosters with a lot of people who have been there longer, so he just needs to be patient and his time will come.

Roxanne Perez is nicknamed The Prodigy for a reason. She is way ahead of the curve on in-ring ability, and that has been the case since she got to WWE.

Unfortunately, she has spent most of her time on the main roster playing backup for Liv Morgan in Judgment Day, which means she hasn't had the level of success she deserves yet.

Being the person WWE can rely on to go out and have a good match with anyone while simultaneously being booked to lose constantly is never an ideal situation for a Superstar.

Roxy is good enough to already be in the world title picture, and hopefully, WWE realizes that and acts accordingly next year.

LA Knight always seems like he is on the cusp of breaking into the main event scene, but for some reason, WWE has yet to commit.

Whenever WWE needs someone for anything, Knight is a good option. He can work heel or babyface, he is good in the ring, even better on the mic, and the crowd loves him.

When Knight was ranting about how he had been kept down in WWE during his feud with Roman Reigns, there was a seed of truth in those words.

The Megastar could easily be elevated at any time, and hopefully, management decides to do it in 2027. He is 44 years old, so he doesn't have forever to work at this level.

Seeing Mark Davis on this list might surprise some people, but if you look at the year he has had, you will understand why.

Dunkzilla is one of those guys who is so good at everything that it often goes unnoticed because we are so used to it.

When AEW booked him to beat Will Ospreay clean, nobody batted an eye at it because it was believable. When he got paired with Jake Doyle, he instantly became one-half of a physically dominant tag team that squashed The Young Bucks in a match.

Davis had a brief national title run, but he deserves so much more success. He is a unique talent with tons of skill and a unique look. There is no reason why he and Doyle should not be holding the tag titles soon.

You might be thinking to yourself, "Chelsea Green was just a WWE champion. How can she possibly be underrated?"

The answer is simple if you look at how she got to that point. During an episode of WWE Unreal, Michael Hayes made comments about Green's booking that upset a lot of her fans because it made it sound like she is only good for putting other women, like Tiffany Stratton, over.

And what just happened? She had a three-month reign with the belt that came to an end at Crown Jewel, thanks to none other than Tiffy.

Green is one of the most versatile women in WWE. She's a hard worker, puts everything she has into even the smallest segments, and is more than willing to look foolish if it helps the story. And on top of all that, she's incredibly entertaining.

The Death Riders are one of a handful of stables in AEW right now, but they are arguably the top faction in the company.

Jon Moxley has had great success, and so have other members of the group, but one guy who often feels like he is only used to give another team a win is Daniel Garcia.

During Anarchy in the Arena at Full Gear, we got to see just how much the crowd loves this guy when he is having fun. As soon as the crowd started hearing DMX and saw Garcia dancing, everyone erupted in cheers.

He's a technical wizard, he's young with a long career ahead of him, and he can be both funny and intimidating. Danny Boy needs a significant push in 2027 to remind everyone how good he is.

Skye Blue is in a very similar situation to Perez in WWE. She is a talented performer who is popular with fans, but she often ends up being sacrificed so someone else can get over.

Blue has become especially known for her willingness to compete in hardcore matches that usually leave her a bloody mess, and she will sometimes wear white gear just to make sure it stands out more.

The good news is at just 27 years old, she still has a ton of time left to find success. By this time next year, she could easily be the TBS champion and nobody would bat an eye because we all know she would be great at it.

Her team with Thekla and Julia Hart is a lot of fun, but if she needs to go off on her own to get what she deserves, then that is what should happen.

Chad Gable is very well regarded for his in-ring ability, and he had a pretty decent 2026 with his first reign as the intercontinental champion, but it took WWE way too long to get here.

Every single match Gable has had for the belt has stolen the show, and his match with El Grande Americano at TripleMania might end up being the best WWE match of the year when it's all wrapped up.

His ability to be comedic while also being a beast in the ring reminds a lot of people of Kurt Angle, and the fact that both men competed in the Olympics on the U.S. wrestling team draws even more comparisons.

If WWE wanted to, it could elevate Gable to the main event scene and nobody would question it. He would make an incredible underdog world champion if given the opportunity.

Athena is still breaking records as the longest-reigning champion in modern pro wrestling, but she is still massively underrated and underused.

The main issue is that this epic reign has taken place in Ring of Honor. AEW rarely uses her on Dynamite or Collision, but when it does, she always knocks it out of the park.

The Fallen Goddess has done an incredible job with this role. There is no denying that at a time when ROH barely feels relevant, she is the one shining light that keeps a lot of fans tuning in every week.

She deserves a bigger stage, bigger opportunities, and more exposure. She is doing the best work of her career, and so few people get to see it because it's behind a paywall.

For a large portion of 2026, Carmela Hayes was having the best matches in WWE every single week on SmackDown against a variety of opponents, but he did not seem to get as many spots on PLEs as one would hope.

He is currently seeing a renewed push after joining up with Royce Keys in 946, and hopefully this feud against The Bloodline elevates everyone in the group.

Melo is one of those performers who just has that extra layer of shine to him. He's so accurate and so precise that it sometimes feels like his reflexes are on a superhuman level.

Hayes has the ability to steal the show at the drop of a hat, and he often does, so let's hope WWE uses him to his fullest potential in 2027.

The 10 men and women on this list are all talented performers who often feel underrated and underused. Who else do you think deserves better booking in WWE and AEW?

articles.title: 5 Trade Ideas for Flyers' Matvei Michkov amid NHL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: The vibes are bad for the Philadelphia Flyers right now.
articles.body:
The vibes are bad for the Philadelphia Flyers right now.

They enter play on Tuesday with a .391 points percentage that is 15th in the Eastern Conference (ahead of only the Columbus Blue Jackets) and 28th in the entire NHL.

Their head coach, Rick Tocchet, is a franchise icon from his playing days and less than a year-and-a-half into his tenure is listening to fans that once cheered for him, calling for him to be fired.

Even worse, one of their most important young players, third-year winger Matvei Michkov, is all of a sudden the subject of rumors after a report surfaced last week that he might want eventually want a fresh start due to the team's losing and some internal turmoil.

Michkov was seen having a tense verbal exchange with teammate Nick Seeler two weeks ago, while he has yet to gain the full trust of two different head coaches (Tocchet and John Tortorella). His ice-time has been inconsistent, he has been a healthy scratch on a few occasions (including in the playoffs a year ago) and his defensive play and conditioning have been major talking points throughout his career.

Even with all of that, he is still an immensely talented player, still only 21 years old, and is the most important young player the organization has due to his upside. He is also the team's leading goal-scorer (11) and point-producer (17) despite being sixth in total ice-time (total minutes played) and seventh in even-strength ice-time per game.

Given the recent report, as well as the rumors that are circulating, and the Flyers' bad start, we're going to at least play the hypothetical game and try to come up with some trade ideas for Michkov.

Would the Flyers Actually Trade Him, and What Would It Look Like?

When going through this exercise you have to keep something very important in mind: There is no indication that Michkov actually requested a trade. Until he does, there is little incentive for the Flyers to move him, or even consider it. They need him to be good, and they need him to be a cornerstone piece of their rebuild. They should be very well aware of that.

The most likely outcome here is that the Flyers eventually make a coaching change, whether it be this season or after the season, and keep trying to develop Michkov.

It is, however, possible that he could pursue an offer sheet as a restricted free agent this offseason, or eventually request a trade, but none of that seems to be on the table right now.

If the Flyers did get concerned about that, it could eventually lead to them preemptively looking for a deal.

If they did, you can be certain that a young center would be at the top of their shopping list. They need a young center that could develop into a top-line player, and they took a huge swing at this past offseason when they signed Leo Carlsson to a five-year offer sheet (The Anaheim Ducks eventually matched it).

First-round picks would also almost certainly be part of the asking price.

We have seen players with lesser resumes and lower ceilings than Michkov get traded for first-round picks (or multiple first-round picks) over the past year.

Florida got a first-round pick for Mackie Samoskevich.

Anaheim got two firsts for Mason McTavish.

New Jersey got two first-round picks for Simon Nemec.

Given that Michkov has already scored at least 20 goals in each of his first two seasons and is currently on a 40-goal pace this season there is no reason they could not expect a young center and at least one first-round pick coming back the other way.

So let's take a look at some ideas with some teams that might be in the market for a young, talented winger with superstar potential.

The Blackhawks are one of the few teams in the NHL worse than the Flyers so far, and it is no secret they are looking to aggressively deal. But they need to be smart about it and not try to salvage a lost season by trading for older veterans that are not going to make a short-term or long-term difference.

They still need to be thinking long-term, and they need to be thinking about giving Connor Bedard more impact players around him.

They missed on the chance to take Ivan Demidov with the No. 2 overall pick in 2024.

Maybe they could help correct that by pursing Michkov if he ever became available. Especially given the trade assets they have to deal from.

The Blackhawks have three first-round picks in 2027, and a couple of young centers with big upside in Anton Frondell and Frank Nazar.

Frondell might be off limits given his upside, but Nazar could absolutely be an option to get moved.

He is not quite as accomplished as Michkov as a player in his young career, and he may not ever be a true No. 1 center, but he could definitely turn into a very good No. 2 center, which would make his $6.59 million salary cap number through the end of the 2032-33 season a bargain.

The trade idea: Chicago trades forward Frank Nazar, a first-round pick, and a prospect to the Flyers for Matvei Michkov.

Expectations are high for Utah this season, and it is not far away from being a legitimate contender in the Western Conference. It also has an aggressive front office that has made bold moves, while also having stockpiled an impressive prospect pool and cupboard full of draft pick assets.

They would be a sensible landing spot for Michkov, and given the prospects they have, a logical trading partner for the Flyers.

At the top of the Utah prospect pool are centers Caleb Desnoyers and Tij Iginla.

While they might not provide the Flyers with immediate help, they would potentially give them a long-term, No. 1 center that could be a building block alongside a player like Porter Martone.

Utah's roster is already really good with a potentially dynamic offense, and adding another high-upside winger would really help brings things together and round out their top-six.

The idea : Utah trades forward prospect Caleb Desnoyers and a future first-round pick to the Flyers for Matvei Michkov.

Ranking the 6 NHL Players Likely to Request a Trade Next

From the moment the Kraken entered the NHL they have been stuck in a perpetual state of mediocrity. Never a contender. Never in a position to get a prime draft pick. No stars. No impact players. No real difference-makers. Just a completely middle-of-the-park, ordinary, mid team.

They not only want to land a star, they are desperate to land one. They just keep failing. But it hasn't been for a lack of effort.

When it comes to their early draft picks, Shane Wright did not pan out and is already traded to the Nashville Predators. Matty Beniers is a very good player, but he is not quite a star player.

They had a trade lined up for Jason Robertson before the NHL Draft, but he turned down their massive contract offer.

You can be sure they will keep trying to take swings whenever a star (or potential star) becomes available. So why wouldn't they want to take a swing for Michkov?

While the NHL roster is short on impact talent, Seattle's farm system does have some really interesting top prospects, including recent first-round picks Chase Reid (defense) and Jake O'Brien (center). They also have four first-round picks over the next three years, including two in 2027. O'Brien is injured at the moment, which could hold back his development a bit in the short-term, but this would not be a trade for the short-term. This would be a much larger long-term move in the hopes of landing a top-line center.

The idea: Seattle trades forward prospect Jake O'Brien, a first-round pick and an additional prospect to the Flyers for Matvei Michkov.

There are messes, and then there is whatever the Detroit Red Wings are right now.

No general manager, an unsigned restricted free agent that is supposed to be a core player, and their longest-tenured captain and long-term captain sitting out of the lineup waiting for a trade that he requested over the summer.

As if that is not enough, the team still is not very good.

So why not try to solve one of those problems while also getting a potential top-line scorer back in return?

The Red Wings may not have the type of young center that the Flyers would be in the market for, but Simon Edvinsson (unsigned restricted free agent) could be a potential top-pairing, long-term option for their defense.

The idea: Detroit trades defenseman Simon Edvinsson to the Flyers for Matvei Michkov.

The Montreal Canadiens have assembled one of the NHL's best young cores, and their Stanley Cup window is just starting to open. So why not try to add to it and really start going for it?

The Canadiens need another top-six scoring winger, and they desperately need some power play help to fix a unit that has been one of the worst in the NHL so far this season.

This is the time where Montreal should be looking to move draft picks and prospects for players that can help it win right now. Especially if it is a player that could potentially be a long-term part of its core. Montreal still has all of its future first-round picks, and a really good farm system of prospects that could be attractive pieces for a rebuilding team. That prospect pool includes center Michael Hage and forward Alexander Zharovsky.

The idea: Montreal trades center MIchael Hage, a first-round pick, and another prospect to the Flyers for Matvei Michkov.

articles.title: 5 Landing Spots for Jordan Binnington Amid NHL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: Over the past two seasons, Jordan Binnington has been the frequent subject of trade rumors. The St. Louis Blues have been rebuilding their roster, prompting speculation that he could be moved to make way for Joel Hofer.
articles.body:
Over the past two seasons, Jordan Binnington has been the frequent subject of trade rumors . The St. Louis Blues have been rebuilding their roster, prompting speculation that he could be moved to make way for Joel Hofer.

Hofer took over the starting goalie role from Binnington last season, and with the latter in the final year of his contract, the Blues could try to move him before the March 1 trade deadline.

It's still too early to say for certain which teams might pursue Binnington before the trade deadline, but we've compiled a list of five possible landing spots.

Despite his struggles in recent years, Binnington has proved himself as a big-game goaltender. He backstopped the Blues to the Stanley Cup in 2018-19, helped Canada win the 2025 4 Nations Face-Off, and got them to the Gold Medal game in the 2026 Winter Olympics.

The 33-year-old is in the final season of a six-year contract carrying a $6 million average annual value. He also has a 10-team no-trade list, giving him some control over where he could be moved.

Despite Binnington's inconsistent play in recent years, he'll be a notable player in next summer's free-agent market. If the Blues become sellers again this season, he could be a player of interest for playoff contenders seeking an experienced netminder.

Jockeying for first place in the overall standings, the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes remain the team to beat this season.

They've had solid goaltending from Pyotr Kochetkov, who's enjoying the best start to a season in his career, with numbers ranking among the best for starting goalies.

Kochetkov seems to have put his previous inconsistent play and last season's injury woes behind him. However, if they flare up again, the Hurricanes might need some help, especially if Brandon Bussi doesn't overcome his rocky start to this season.

Hurricanes general manager Eric Tulsky isn't afraid to make bold moves if necessary. Binnington could be an option if Kochetkov and Bussi struggle during the second half of the season.

The Hurricanes currently have over $9.7 million in cap space, which will continue to accrue as the season progresses, giving them more than enough to absorb Binnington's $6 million cap hit. They also have plenty of draft picks and could draw on their prospect pipeline as trade bait if needed.

The Edmonton Oilers entered this season with Tristan Jarry and Devon Levi as their goaltending tandem because a knee injury sidelined offseason acquisition Frederik Andersen. Jarry's consistency has improved, while the inexperienced Levi has seized the opportunity to prove himself as a reliable NHL goalie.

The Oilers don't need a rental goalie right now. However, it might become necessary if Jarry's inconsistency returns, Levi struggles as the season goes on, and Andersen is slow to regain his form whenever he rejoins the lineup.

One observer believes the Oilers could use a more seasoned starter like Binnington. On Nov. 7, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that he'd heard "some noise" about the Blues' goaltender in the trade market. Guest panelist Erik Johnson felt the Oilers should pursue him.

Two days later, Friedman brought up Binnington on his 32 Thoughts podcast . He doesn't believe the Oilers are looking into it because they're pleased with their current tandem, but he didn't rule it out.

The New York Rangers experienced a setback on Oct. 9 when starting goaltender Igor Shesterkin suffered a season-ending leg injury during a game against the Washington Capitals.

Losing the former Vezina Trophy winner left them with an inexperienced Dylan Garand and a banged-up Joonas Korpisalo as their tandem.

Garand has exceeded expectations thus far, while Korpisalo has looked good since returning from a foot injury that had sidelined him since the preseason. They also cycled through Spencer Martin and James Reimer until Korpisalo's return.

The Rangers will likely stick with Garand and Korpisalo for as long as they keep getting the job done. However, a serious injury or performance setback for either goalie could send them into the trade market for help, especially if they're in contention for a playoff berth.

On Nov. 15, the Rangers placed Shesterkin on season-ending long-term injury reserve, giving them over $9 million in salary cap space . That's more than enough room to pursue Binnington if necessary. They could offer up one of their extra third-round picks in 2027 or 2028 in return.

Ranking the 6 NHL Players Likely to Request a Trade Next

Trade Ideas for Matvei Michkov amid NHL Trade Rumors

During the offseason, the Toronto Maple Leafs overhauled their front office, changed their coaching staff, and shook up their roster with several moves, including signing veteran goaltender Sergei Bobrovsky.

While better on paper, they're still struggling on the ice and sit near the bottom of the standings.

Bobrovsky's shaky goaltending could push the Maple Leafs to lean more heavily on backup Anthony Stolarz. They could use help between the pipes, but their current-season cap constraints would complicate a move for Binnington.

The Maple Leafs' priority is their blue-line depth, so they're unlikely to seek a goaltending upgrade with their current tandem healthy. Acquiring Binnington is a long shot, but one the Maple Leafs could look into if the opportunity arises.

If Bobrovsky ($7 million average annual value) or Stolarz ($3.8 million) is sidelined with a long-term injury, the Maple Leafs could have the cap space to pursue someone like Binnington. However, they could still require the Blues to retain half of his $6 million cap hit.

Following a solid October performance, the Utah Mammoth have struggled in November.

Injuries to key players such as Logan Cooley, Dylan Guenther, and Nick Schmaltz haven't helped, but there's also growing concern about the form of starting goaltender Karel Vejmelka.

Vejmelka has been a regular starter for Arizona and Utah since entering the NHL in 2021. He won 38 games last season, helping Utah reach the playoffs for the first time in franchise history.

However, the 30-year-old is struggling, with stats that rank among the worst for starting goalies. That could force Mammoth general manager Bill Armstrong into the trade market for someone like Binnington, whose numbers could improve with a change of scenery.

The Mammoth will have over $12 million in accrued cap space by the March 1 trade deadline. They also have extra draft picks to offer the Blues, particularly if St. Louis retains up to half of Binnington's cap hit.

One downside is that they would have to carry three goalies because backup Sebastian Cossa is no longer waiver-exempt.

articles.title: Cody Rhodes vs. CM Punk Feud Coming Soon, Cruz Montana Gets WWE Stamp of Approval, More Raw Fallout
articles.summary: The November 16 edition of Raw on Netflix continued the build to Survivor Series: WarGames from the Lenovo Center in Raleigh, North Carolina.
articles.body:
The November 16 edition of WWE Raw on Netflix continued the build to Survivor Series: WarGames from the Lenovo Center in Raleigh, North Carolina.

Iyo Sky dethroned Raquel Rodriguez to become the new women's intercontinental champion. Cruz Montana picked up a big win with Carmelo Hayes over The Usos.

Cody Rhodes and CM Punk recruited LA Knight to Team USA. Jacy Jayne took a disqualification loss to Stephanie Vaquer before Fatal Influence beat down their WarGames rivals.

Check out the fallout from Raw below, setting the stage for what can be expected at Survivor Series.

Cody Rhodes and CM Punk Gearing Up for a Monster Feud

Team USA vs. Team Mexico is a central story for Survivor Series that lacks real stakes. The only real drama is who will join each team.

With those teams, though, it is fair to ask what the ultimate goal of this traditional Survivor Series elimination match is.

The answer may come down to the aftermath involving Team USA's two captains.

WWE has long teased Rhodes vs. Punk, but the story has not come together. This is the first time these two men are working together week after week.

It seems like WWE wants these two connected for a while after this story, which makes sense as a strong feud for WrestleMania 43.

If Team USA falls short due to miscommunications, it could be the beginning of Rhodes and Punk fighting on a big stage.

This would be a logical next step after Rhodes' feuds with John Cena and Randy Orton heading into the last two WrestleManias, giving The American Nightmare a chance to show off the edge he has developed while fighting Punk's peers.

WWE Going Overboard With Roxanne Perez Teases

Becky Lynch delivered two impactful lines during her roast of Liv Morgan that felt like pointed critiques of current WWE booking.

First, she called out how much Dominik Mysterio has cooled off since WrestleMania 41.

Second, she declared Roxanne Perez the most talented wrestler in The Judgment Day despite Perez having no championship to show for her recent efforts.

Both statements have been made in the past to some extent, but it is hard to hear both articulated so clearly without any plan to change these fumbles into future success.

Most importantly right now, WWE cannot keep saying that The Prodigy is great while booking her to lose at every hurdle.

Time and again, WWE has told fans that Perez is the future and a star in the making, but her failures make those statements seem irrelevant.

The easiest answer would be to heat her up with a Royal Rumble win followed by a Liv challenge in the vein of Batista's WrestleMania 21 journey.

However, if all of this is just to get cheap pops for The Man, there is no point even calling it out.

The Judgment Day was once WWE's most formidable heel faction, but the talented remnants of that group are likely only to find success by walking away.

It would be easy to forget Jacy Jayne is the women's United States champion if she didn't carry the title around with her.

Since winning the gold, Fatal Influence's leading lady has defended the gold once, just one week after capturing the title.

She is approaching 100 days without a title defense—the same drought for which Liv Morgan was criticized during her much-maligned world title reign.

It is not as if Jayne has been off television. She has wrestled six matches in that time, but she lost her last two one-on-one contests without her gold on the line.

If WWE wants fans to take Jayne seriously as a rising heel, she cannot keep taking losses and carrying around her gold as an accessory.

WWE needs to be willing to give her wins against stars like Charlotte Flair and Stephanie Vaquer rather than taking messy losses that make Jayne look like the lesser act.

Predicting Final Members of Team USA and Team Mexico 🔮

While Jacy Jayne's Women's United States Championship reign has been a disappointment, there is still time to recover it.

Raquel Rodriguez's Women's Intercontinental Championship reign has ended after 112 days with just one successful title defense.

Despite the promising start of a title reign worthy of a veteran who had proved her worth, the championship was as much a prop for Big Mami Cool as Morgan's world title was for her.

Iyo Sky cannot follow the same path. The Genius of the Sky is the best wrestler in WWE, and the company should lean into that.

A monthly title defense should be the minimum for Sky, who can deliver must-see television on Raw during her reign.

Perhaps Sky will be the first star since Becky Lynch to make fans care about the Women's Intercontinental Championship.

If the goal was just to give Sky something to do, though, the title should have gone to a younger star while keeping The Genius of the Sky ready for another world title run.

WWE Goes All-In on Cruz Montana With Win in Raw Main Event Debut

Cruz Montana's first official match on the main roster saw him pin Jey Uso in the center of the ring.

Less than four months after making his NXT debut, Montana pinned a former world heavyweight champion in the main event of Raw.

That is a ringing endorsement for the quick NXT call-up, who suddenly looks like a real threat to The Bloodline.

If this booking continues, Montana could rise up the ranks even faster than Royce Keys.

It was a necessary move for 946, who need to look like real problems for anyone in WWE to deal with if they are going to hurt The Bloodline.

While 946 has been booked big since forming, it is still an alliance of rookies from the perspective of main-roster success fighting the biggest stable in modern WWE.

Wins like this could even help 946 overcome a loss inside WarGames as long as Montana, Keys, Carmelo Hayes, OTM and Jaida Parker begin picking up big wins on Raw going forward.

articles.title: Ranking the 6 NHL Players Likely to Request a Trade Next
articles.summary: We've been reeling all season long from the number of superstar NHL players who have asked to be traded. Going back to the offseason with Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin and now into the season with Nikita Kucherov, it's staggering to see so many elite players express displeasure with where they are and wanting out.
articles.body:
We've been reeling all season long from the number of superstar NHL players who have asked to be traded. Going back to the offseason with Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin and now into the season with Nikita Kucherov, it's staggering to see so many elite players express displeasure with where they are and wanting out.

All while we're witnessing this change of philosophy by players and stars seeking to take control of their situations, we're left wondering... Who's next to ask for a trade?

Now that we're about 20 games into the season and we're starting to see the haves and have-nots starting to establish themselves, we're keeping our eyes fixed on the teams that are falling far back of the packs in their conferences to scout for possibilities.

Some of our choices are based on recent history while others are tied into where their contracts are and when they're expiring. We're kicking ideas around here and wondering aloud if maybe these stars might take inspiration from current trends.

Let's theorize what a situation where Auston Matthews asked for a trade out of Toronto could look like and what it would mean.

Matthews is captain of the Maple Leafs and their best player and unfortunately, the Leafs are struggling to stay close to their rivals in the Atlantic Division and Eastern Conference yet again. After being part of some great teams that couldn't get over the hump for more than a few seasons in Toronto, the Leafs are looking at potentially being out of the mix for the playoffs again.

Toronto missing the playoffs would normally mean looking ahead to the draft lottery, something that allowed them to luck out and land Gavin McKenna in the 2026 Draft with the No. 1 pick. But the Leafs won't have their own first-round pick in 2027 or 2028 thanks to previous trades. Matthews has one more year left on his contract after this season before potentially becoming an unrestricted free agent and you can see why this situation could get gnarly.

If Matthews wanted a trade, he'd have full control over where he could go thanks to a no-move clause. Aside from the major psychic damage that would come from such a situation for the Leafs, Toronto could look at this as a way to majorly recoup futures (first-round picks, top prospects) and still have a potentially elite player in McKenna to replace Matthews on hand already.

If things keep sliding away for Toronto, you have to wonder if Matthews would want to ride it out or not. Heck, you could make the same argument for William Nylander with the big difference being that his contract goes until 2032.

We've already seen Artemi Panarin get traded a year ago when the New York Rangers sent him to the Los Angeles Kings. While Panarin enjoyed the move enough to sign a two-year extension to stay with L.A., we're guessing he wasn't expecting to see the Kings wind up near the bottom of the Western Conference when he did so.

Panarin is 35 years old and his two-year, $22 million extension isn't exactly cheap. But given his history of offensive production and his continued solid production this season (19 points in 17 games), if the Breadman wanted to get out of Los Angeles to join a more competitive team, who could blame him?

The Kings are in a bit of an awkward transition following Anže Kopitar's retirement and with Drew Doughty at 36 years old in a contract year. They're also a very veteran team and for the handful of top younger players they have (Quinton Byfield, Brandt Clarke), they need more. If Panarin were to ask out, trading him could help make that happen.

We know it feels like Elias Pettersson's name has been in trade rumors for a long time and while that's cooled off since J.T. Miller was traded to the Rangers in February 2025, it has to be tough for Pettersson to see the Canucks be among the league's worst teams yet again this season.

If Pettersson were to want out of Vancouver with five more years left on his contract with an $11.6 million cap hit, it would be equally deflating and sad to see as it would be fascinating to see how that trade would get put together.

This season, Pettersson has had a bit of a return to glory putting up a point per game (23 points in 23 games) after producing at 0.7 points per game the previous two seasons combined. Seeing his production pick up again despite the team's struggles is notable, especially given how much he struggled previously and how foreboding that seemed. A Pettersson resurgence would no doubt help get more teams to the table even with his bulky contract.

Trade Ideas for Matvei Michkov amid NHL Trade Rumors

We don't mean to pick on the Canucks, but when a team has struggled as much as they have the past few seasons and with the amount of rumors that swirled, it's inevitable. One of those guys who's been in rumors is Jake DeBrusk and if the power forward wanted to escape Vancouver, there's no doubt the market for him would be busy.

DeBrusk carries a $5.5 million cap hit and a contract that has four more years beyond this one which makes him more than affordable, especially with the cap skyrocketing in coming years. He's scored 20-plus goals in four of the past five seasons and while he's got just 12 points in 21 games this season, his rugged style of play would make him a favorite anywhere in the league.

Given that DeBrusk is 30 years old, that comes with the usual "buyer beware" caveats, especially with him being signed through 2031, his style of play and ability to get to the net would make him plenty attractive. His no-move clause this season would also allow him to pick where he wanted to go...if he wanted to leave.

There are a lot of reasons to be bummed out about seeing the Pittsburgh Penguins struggling. Watching superstar veteran players struggle is hard to see and the possibility of those players missing out on the postseason instead of getting one more crack at a Stanley Cup is sad. While we doubt any of Sidney Crosby, Evgeni Malkin or Kris Letang would ask for a trade to go for a shot at one more Stanley Cup, we can't say the same for Erik Karlsson who's still looking for his first.

Karlsson is in the final year of his contract and even though his cap hit is still juicy at $10 million and he has a full no-move clause, he can still play well, move the puck and produce offense from the blue line. He leads the Penguins with 19 points this season (in 20 games) with eight of those points coming on the power play.

Contending teams would love to add a player like Karlsson to make them deeper and it's possible (likely?) that he wouldn't even need to ask for a trade to be moved this season. GM Kyle Dubas has done well with trades the past few seasons and if a contender calls for Karlsson, the only thing that would get in the way of him getting his asking price would be Karlsson nixing the move.

You have to wonder what's going through Zach Werenski's mind these days.

After an awkward offseason in which he initially asked to be traded and then walked it back after speaking with Blue Jackets management, the 2026 Norris Trophy winner is playing well on a Columbus team that's sunk to the bottom of the Eastern Conference and fighting for air.

Werenski has one more year left on his contract with the Jackets before he can become an unrestricted free agency and with the way Columbus is struggling, you wouldn't be able to blame Werenski if he was already reassessing his desire to stay there.

An elite No. 1 defenseman hitting the trade market would create a frenzy, but Werenski's no-move clause means he would be able to select his destination of choice. Curiously enough, PuckPedia.com shows that Werenski's no-move changes to a 10-team trade list next season. If Werenski pulls the trigger and says he wants out, it would create a potentially fascinating situation.

articles.title: Brazil defeat Singapore 7-0 as Vinicius scores first-half hat-trick
articles.summary: Brazil’s star forward scored a 12-minute hat-trick in the record world champions’ thumping of the hosts in a friendly.
articles.body:
Vinicius Junior hit a 12-minute hat-trick in the first half as Brazil turned on the style in a 7-0 trouncing of Singapore in an international friendly.

Endrick, Estevao, Rayan and substitute Allan also found the net as the South Americans brushed aside their hosts with a dominant performance at the National Stadium on Tuesday.

Brazil were much changed from their 3-2 loss to Japan on Saturday , in which manager Carlo Ancelotti and captain Raphinha were shown red cards, with Vinicius one of only four players retaining their places in the starting lineup.

Bruno Guimaraes took over as skipper and set up the opener after nine minutes, playing a quick pass to Vinicius, who wrong-footed Singapore captain Hariss Harun with his first touch before dispatching a left-footed shot past goalkeeper Izwan Mahbud.

The Real Madrid forward notched his second in the 15th minute after a quick counterattack by the Selecao as Endrick laid the ball off for his unmarked teammate to slot home.

Vinicius was denied by Izwan shortly afterwards, but he completed his hat-trick in the 21st minute when he was found completely unmarked in the six-yard box by Estevao’s low centre.

Rayan had an effort disallowed for offside, but Endrick added to Brazil’s lead in the 31st minute with a low effort from range that found the bottom right corner.

Estevao also had a goal disallowed for a foul by Vinicius, but the Chelsea winger added to Brazil’s tally just after the interval with a deflected shot from the edge of the box.

Rayan rocked the crossbar soon after, but the endeavour of the Bournemouth forward was rewarded in the 65th minute when he rounded substitute goalkeeper Syazwan Buhari to make it 6-0.

Brazil rang the changes in the closing stages, and Allan came off the bench to grab the seventh goal in the 74th minute with a low-angled shot that nicked off Raoul Suhaimi on its way into the net.

articles.title: CBS Sports Forecasts Texas A&M To Move On From Marcel Reed In 2027
articles.summary: CBS Sports predicts Texas A&M will replace Marcel Reed in 2027. See why the Aggies are moving on and what this means for the program.
articles.body:
CBS Sports predicts Texas A&M will not start Marcel Reed at quarterback in 2027. The outlet says the Aggies will use the transfer portal to find a new starter. This move comes after a rough season where the offense struggled to score points and the team lost key games.

The 2026 season showed clear signs that the current quarterback and play-caller combination is not working. Texas A&M lost to Tennessee 22-7 on a Saturday in November. The team only gained 179 total yards in that game. Reed threw for just 71 yards and one interception before being replaced by backup Brady Hart. CBS Sports's Brad Crawford wrote that the time for Reed as the starter is over.

Third-year coach Mike Elko faces pressure to fix the offense. The team sits at 4-6 overall and 1-6 in the SEC. Holmon Wiggins, the first-year offensive coordinator, and Joey Lynch, the quarterbacks coach, have failed to aid Reed's progress. During conference games, Reed managed just two touchdowns while tossing eight interceptions. He also missed games or was benched due to poor performance.

Wiggins has called plays that lack creativity. The offense failed to score a touchdown in three SEC games. CBS Sports says the ship has sailed on Reed. The analysis points out that keeping the same quarterback and coordinator for a third year makes little sense. The Aggies need a player who can move the chains and throw the ball well on third downs.

Elko has the money to spend to get a new quarterback. Texas A&M has a financial edge that could help them land a top player from the transfer portal. The school does not have to settle for a backup or an unproven player. They can find a starter who has played well at another big school.

During the loss to Tennessee, Elko explained why he stopped calling designed runs for Reed. He said the offense was never built around the quarterback running the ball. Many people think running is Reed's best skill, but Elko disagrees.

Elko noted that Reed's best runs come when he scrambles or pulls the ball on zone reads. He believes other teams now know this and stop those plays. "He pulls the ball on zone reads. That's where he gets his runs. He scrambles. I just think teams are aware of that, and they're not letting him do it," Elko added.

This explanation shows why the offense looks one-dimensional. Wiggins, who used to coach wide receivers, calls plays that rely on receivers running perfect routes. This style does not fit a dual-threat quarterback like Reed. Former coordinator Collin Klein knew how to use Reed's running skills better.

Choosing a new quarterback is only half the battle. Texas A&M must also decide if Holmon Wiggins stays as the offensive coordinator. Elko has shown loyalty to Wiggins even after bad losses. However, Wiggins has not fixed the scoring problems.

If Wiggins stays, top quarterbacks in the portal might not want to come to Texas A&M. They may not trust the system. Names like Austin Mack from Alabama and Ethan Grunkemeyer from Virginia Tech are linked to the Aggies. These players are proven starters who need a scheme that fits their skills.

CBS Sports argues that the play-caller decision is more important than the quarterback choice. Investing in a new passer requires a coach who can help him win at an elite level. Sticking with Wiggins could hurt the chances of landing a top recruit. The fan base is tired of waiting for Year 3 of the same plan.

The Aggies have the resources to rebuild the offense quickly. They can afford to bring in a new quarterback and a new coordinator if needed. The goal is to find a tandem that works together from day one. This approach avoids the learning curve of a new system.

Elko and athletic director Trev Alberts must act fast. The transfer portal moves quickly, and good players get signed early. If the staff waits too long, the best options will be gone. A quarterback capable of maintaining the offense's rhythm is essential for the team.

Reed's regression is a clear sign that a change is needed. Although he posted a career-best 25 touchdowns and 3,169 yards last season, his statistics declined this year. Mechanical issues and bad decisions have plagued him. Wiggins has not been able to fix these problems.

The Aggies have the money and the need to find a new leader for the offense. Several recognizable names are available in the portal, but the scheme matters most. If Wiggins remains, the pool of willing quarterbacks shrinks. The decision on the coordinator will shape the 2027 season more than the player on the field.

Fans in College Station have seen a drop in offensive production. In multiple categories, the team is near the SEC's lowest ranks. Keeping the same staff and quarterback would mean more of the same struggles. A change offers hope for a better season.

The financial power of Texas A&M is a major asset. It allows the program to compete for the best talent in the country. Using this advantage to fix the quarterback and coordinator spots could turn the program around quickly.

Elko's loyalty to Wiggins is the biggest question mark. The coach must decide if the coordinator deserves another year. The answer to that question will determine if the Aggies can land a top-tier quarterback.

articles.summary: The Detroit Red Wings remain steadfast in their lack of movement in a Dylan Larkin trade. So far, none of […]
articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings remain steadfast in their lack of movement in a Dylan Larkin trade. So far, none of the teams on Larkin's list have presented an offer to move the needle for Shawn Horcoff and Detroit. Whether appetite for the 30+ goal scorer has increased around the league is hard to say for certain in Hockeytown as the mercurial center apparently remains committed to his list.

The Red Wings, of course, aren't looking to make a lateral move, and if a team wants to get a player like Larkin, they'll have to give up a player, who, like Larkin, has the offensive ability to take over a game skating in the top six. That, unfortunately, is an ask that's hard for teams already in their contention window who don't want to decrease their odds of winning now or lengthen the timeline of a potential rebuild.

What that means in reality is a proven veteran or an up-and-coming forward who fits into Detroit's current crop of youngsters like Czech netminder Michal Postava on the timeline for Detroit's own contention.

Across the sea in Postava's home country, legendary Penguins forward Jaromir Jagr appears to have finally hung his skates up. According to a report from TSN , Jagr spoke with Zdeněk Janda of Czech sports media outlet iSport.cz Monday.

"Your body will always tell you. If you listen to it, it will tell you that the time is right. If you have nothing more to give and you feel like you're doing more harm than good, it's time to leave. But I think I've squeezed every last drop out of it." The 54-year-old Jagr said in the interview with Janda, who helped write his memoir "JÁ68.

There are no winners in the war between the Red Wings and RFA Simon Edvinsson.

Griffins center Theo Rochette may be returning to his homeland.

The Red Wings probably aren't the team for you if you're a betting man.

In 1979 Mr. Hockey found himself squaring off The Great One while playing for the Hartford Whalers in the NHL. Gordie Howe earned his moniker of "Mr. Hockey" playing for the Red Wings but did spend a few years in the WHA after his first retirement from the NHL after defining the old era of the professional game.

Wayne Gretzky meanwhile, would go on to define the way that hockey has been played through the WHA's merger with the NHL and his storied career playing for the Edmonton Oilers, LA Kings, St. Louis Blues, and New York Rangers.

articles.title: Report card grades for every NFC team in NFL Week 10
articles.summary: Grading every NFC team that played in Week 10 of the NFL season.
articles.body:
Week 10 of the NFL season has wrapped up, featuring significant victories for the Lions, Rams, and 49ers. The Giants faced a tough loss in a divisional clash against Washington, while the Vikings showcased their strength by overpowering the Packers at Lambeau Field. Below are the report card grades in the NFC for Week 10.

The Detroit Lions dominated the Patriots in Spain, and this offense is elite. Jahmyr Gibbs is the best running back in football, and the Lions are going to continue feeding him. This defense has turned the corner as well after being one of the worst in football. The bad news: Aidan Hutchinson suffered a severe knee injury after celebrating.

The Vikings have their QB, and it is a familiar face in Kirk Cousins, but this is exactly what the team needed. A stable passer who can get the ball out fast, and then their defense will hold their opponents. This team is an elite contender now that they have better QB play moving forward.

The Packers went down early to the Vikings, and their offensive line got beat up by Brian Flores's defense. A rough showing for Green Bay, as they only put points in the 3rd quarter. In this NFC North, losses are becoming bigger than they are because of how good this division is.

The Chicago Bears hit the bye this week and regroup as they take on the New Orleans Saints at home.

The Rams offense, despite having injuries to numerous receivers, was able to get it done, and Blake Corum has been awesome for the Rams. Another great week from him. A big win over the Cardinals, 34-6.

The 49ers offense came to play in Dallas, with Christian McCaffrey having a monster day in the receiving game. Brock Purdy showed out in this NFC clash against the Cowboys. The defense struggled to contain George Pickens, but this was still a big win for them.

The Seahawks secured a crucial victory against the Raiders, keeping their playoff hopes alive. Jaxon Smith-Njigba delivered another outstanding performance, playing a pivotal role in the offense. However, the run game requires enhancement, as defenses are likely to adapt to the passing strategy.

The Cardinals' offense under Carson Beck struggled, and they will continue to struggle with injuries to their key weapons. Their receivers are not great, and they will need to get more out of their weapons if they want this offense to be semi-productive.

The Cowboys defense is the main story in this high-scoring battle. Christian Parker's defense allowed over 500 total yards. They could not stop anything, and he is going to be out of a job very soon. George Pickens was very good in a bounce-back game. But this Dallas team could not take advantage after the Giants lost to the Commanders. This team is fully healthy and is in 1st place in the NFC East.

The Giants were in the driver's seat after picking off Jayden Daniels for a second time. Less than 2:30 left in the game, and all they had to do was pick up a first down or two, and the play-calling failed them. A rough game, as they have a tough game next week versus Jacksonville.

The Commanders played a decent game, but their defense and coaching outclassed the Giants late in this game. A great play call to Stefon Diggs sealed the game and spoiled the whiteout game from the New York Giants. A big win, and the NFC East is anyone's game still.

The Eagles were on bye this week, and this team needed a reset. They will take on the Pittsburgh Steelers, who struggled against the Bengals

The Panthers win a close game against the Saints, but this team has problems. Bryce Young didn't have his great stuff, but Chuba Hubbard is a phenomenal player. His upside gets even higher with him in the pass game. Overall, a much-needed win for the Panthers.

The Saints found a way to lose another close game. Their run game is invisible, while Jordyn Tyson had a solid performance. The division is wide open. Which team is going to rise and win this tight NFC South?

The Buccaneers were on bye this week and will head to Detroit next week to take on Jahmyr Gibbs and the Lions.

The Falcons faced a formidable Chiefs team and put forth a strong effort. However, the Chiefs showcased their dominance throughout the game. The Falcons struggled to contain the Chiefs' explosive offense, with Patrick Mahomes effectively exploiting weaknesses in their defense. Given their current performance, Atlanta appears to have a challenging road ahead in this competitive division.

articles.title: Dodgers notes: DH possibilities, the pitch to Tarik Skubal
articles.summary: Much has been made so far this offseason about Shohei Ohtani’s future playing capacity for the Los Angeles Dodgers – whether he should pitch, if so how much,...
articles.body:
Much has been made so far this offseason about Shohei Ohtani's future playing capacity for the Los Angeles Dodgers – whether he should pitch, if so how much, etc.

In his piece for MLB.com, Mike Petriello outlines how the unicorn that is Ohtani complicates building a roster around him.

In the article, Petriello cites three specific issues with having a permanent DH that is named Ohtani, and their current roster construction – having the oldest corner infielders in the league, their best rising star is also a DH, and that Dalton Rushing isn't ready to catch again yet but can hit.

Petriello says there are two things that the Dodgers could do about it – Let Josue De Paula play left field, and move Tommy Edman back to a utility player role, spelling those aging players. Petriello also notes that this is most likely the last season the Dodgers would have to deal with the current makeup of the team, as both Max Muncy and Freddie Freeman's contracts will be up at the end of the 2027 season.

If there's any team that can be creative with their roster, we know it will be the Dodgers.

Jack Harris of the California Post posits that the Dodgers will not be offering Tarik Skubal a big long-term contract, as they have to many big-name free agents in the past, but should instead work on convincing the two-time Cy Young winner a higher, but shorter term contract.

The New York Mets, Toronto Blue Jays, and San Diego Padres seem to be the Dodgers' biggest competitors to land Skubal, but as Harris points out, those teams also will be wary of handing out a huge contract as they have been burned by them in the past.

articles.title: Brighton Fixtures Preview: What to Expect From the Next Games
articles.summary: Fabian Hurzeler battles a winless December curse as Albion face eleven pivotal clashes. From European tests to domestic hurdles, can the Seagulls finally mas...
articles.body:
As we know, the upcoming Christmas period is a very busy time in the football world. Transfers, games coming thick and fast, load management, the lot.

And, given Brighton's previous record in December under Fabian Hurzeler, it makes a grim reading, and understandably brings some pessimism.

For context, Albion have never won a game in Hurzeler's time at the club, in the month of December.

Hurzeler's side face 11 fixtures in the runup to the new year, and on paper, these seem favourable, but I won't speak too soon…

In order: Hull (a), Craiova (H), Newcastle (H), Bournemouth (a), Forest (A), Monaco (H), Everton (H), Panathinaikos (A), Ipswich (H), Fulham (A), Spurs (A).

In my opinion, every single game here is winnable. But, knowing Brighton, we could well end up with ZERO wins, like the previous two years.

Going through each game and based on other teams' form, we should be looking to win every game here. The most difficult being David Moyes' Everton.

Newcastle and Ipswich should be wins, with Newcastle struggling so far this season. Ipswich will not be an easy game; well-coached and difficult to beat under Gary O'Neil.

Everton at home has traditionally been a difficult game, losing 5-1, and 1-0 in the past, and drawing plenty, including a 1-1 draw last season, which saw pressure mounted on Fabian Hurzeler.

Two crucial games in our campaign to finish in the top eight of the Conference League 'League stage', against Universitea Craiova and AS Monaco.

Monaco are one of the (on paper) hardest games in our quest to qualify for the knockouts in the whole of the UEFA Conference League.

Filipe Luis' side started the season very well, being top of the league at one stage, but have since fallen off a cliff in form, dropping to seventh.

Only one game awaits the Albion in the Conference League in terms of away fixtures, and that is another trip to Athens for the Albion faithful.

Starting with Hull, a side who since going unbeaten in their first few outings with impressive results, have also dropped off massively.

But one way or another, Sergej Jakirovic' side are tough to beat. Plenty of physicality, and approach opposition very well.

Bournemouth, a team who have found their rhythm under new boss Marco Rose, the most difficult game in this whole month, especially given our previous record away to the Dorset based side.

Nottingham Forest have struggled for form on paper, but their underlying numbers suggest that they should be within the top five. Another winnable, but very difficult game against Oliver Glasner's side, who Fabian has never beaten…

Fulham away, not much needs to be said really. Last time at the Cottage, a superb performance for 80 minutes, until Hurzeler's substitutions ruined the flow of the game.

And finally, a second reunion with ex gaffer Roberto De Zerbi awaits for the travelling Seagulls fans, to finish off an intense month.

Spurs have seen a big improvement since the start of the season, and we know full well what a Roberto De Zerbi team is capable of.

But I feel good. The fanbase feels good. The squad, the club, the moment, feels good. We are very hopeful of another successful month, and one that is crucial in the context of our season.

Bayer Leverkusen have made further progress in their efforts to extend Ibrahim Maza's contract, with talks now in the final stages, according to Sky Germany.

The Algeria international is set to extend his current deal by a further year, taking it from 2030 until 2031, with no release clause to be included in the agreement.

The move would put Die Werkself in an even stronger negotiating position amid growing interest in the 20-year-old, with Sky Germany adding that the Bundesliga club expect to sell him by the summer of 2028 at the latest.

Leverkusen reportedly view Maza as their next potential €100 million-plus sale.

articles.title: “They Really Thought He Couldn’t Play Anymore”: Rob Parker Snubs Patrick Mahomes To Anoint Deshaun Watson As Comeback Player of the Year
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson has been one of the NFL’s most criticized players since being traded to the Cleveland Browns in 2022. That said, he may be on track to rehabil...
articles.body:
Deshaun Watson has been one of the NFL's most criticized players since being traded to the Cleveland Browns in 2022. That said, he may be on track to rehabilitate his image this year.

On Sunday against the Houston Texans, the Cleveland Browns quarterback underperformed in the air, not throwing a single touchdown and being intercepted once. However, he was also one of three players who had a rushing touchdown in the 27-24 victory, which ended a two-game skid.

That performance prompted high praise from ESPN's Stephen A. Smith, who wrote on social media :

"What a comeback by (Deshaun Watson) (The NFL Comeback Player of the Year, as far as I'm concerned) and the Browns. What a 2nd Half Show."

On Monday's episode of the Fox Sports Radio podcast The Odd Couple , co-host Rob Parker concurred with Smith. He named Watson his choice for Comeback Player of the Year, notably passing over Patrick Mahomes in the process:

"Patrick Mahomes is not the Comeback Player of the Year. … They really thought this guy, who was an all-pro player, was going to give up and roll over into a ball, and he couldn't play anymore. …They mocked me for saying he could still play! Watson will be one of the GREATEST comeback stories EVER!"

Deshaun Watson's former AFC South rival calls for Browns to re-sign QB after 2026 season

Deshaun Watson's resurgence comes amid speculation regarding his future, as he is in the final year of the historic $230-million contract that he signed in 2022.

On Sunday's episode of the 4th and South podcast, co-host and former running back Leonard Fournette, who spent the first three years of his career with the Jacksonville Jaguars, the rival of Watson's former team, the Houston Texans, made his case for the Browns to give the quarterback a new contract in 2027 (discussion begins at 32:10 in the video below):

"He's playing like a QB1 and a future QB1. It's hard to find quarterbacks in this league nowadays. He had his ups and downs, but he's comfortable right now."

Watson and the Browns are now in their bye week. They next host the Las Vegas Raiders on Nov. 29. Kickoff is at 1 p.m. ET on Fox.

articles.title: Andorra owner Gerard Pique says Jesus Owono doesn’t deserve ban after footballer’s death
articles.summary: Owono has been suspended for 12 matches after colliding with De Miguel during a Spanish second-tier match
articles.body:
Andorra owner Gerard Pique believes that goalkeeper Jesus Owono does not deserve the 12-match ban he received following the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel .

Owono collided with De Miguel in stoppage time of a Spanish second-tier match on 2 November, with De Miguel subsequently rushed to intensive care before passing away the morning after in hospital.

Owono, who was sent off for the foul before the match was abandoned, said he was going through "the most difficult days of my life" in the aftermath of De Miguel's death.

He has since been hit with a lengthy suspension for violent conduct by the Spanish football federation (Rfef), with its disciplinary committee saying he used "excessive force" in the collision.

This has drawn the ire of former Barcelona defender Pique, the majority shareholder of Owono's club Andorra, who feels the Equatorial Guinea stopper is being punished for the consequences rather than his action.

"Players, ​former ⁠players, coaches, goalkeepers, everyone has called it an accident," Pique said in a video posted on social media ⁠late on Monday.

"I truly believe that imposing the maximum sanction on Jesus for this action puts him in a situation he does not deserve, because he is not to blame for all of this having happened."

Pique says there is inconsistency in the punishment, citing Albacete winger Jose Corpas' three-match ban after his high challenge on Sabadell midfielder Quadri Liameed left him hospitalised.

"Fortunately Quadri is fine, the consequences in this case were not fatal, and the committee decided to sanction Corpas with three matches," he added.

"With all this, my reflection is: what is being sanctioned, the action or the consequences?"

Andorra general manager Jaume Nogues told Andorra Radio and Television on Tuesday that they would not be appealing the disciplinary committee's decision, but that their resolution on the case was "not done well".

Nogues said an appeal would be "frowned upon socially", adding that Owono was also not in favour of launching an appeal.

Meanwhile, Tenerife manager Alvaro Cervera ‌did not agree with Pique's evaluation.

"He has to defend his players and his club, and he clearly believes thats what hes doing," Cervera told a press conference on Tuesday.

"I do think the action [Owono's ⁠challenge] could have been avoided. I don't believe this is the kind of action ⁠we see every day, despite what he seems to be suggesting."

Spanish police opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter.

Under Spanish law, deaths from non-natural causes, including accidents, are subject to judicial investigation, though prosecutors have said that criminal proceedings are unlikely.

Andorra coach Carles Manso said it will be up to Owono to decide when he feels ready to play again, with Pique stating that Owono will live with the repercussions of the incident for much longer than the duration of his 12-game suspension.

"Jesus is going to need far more than 12 matches before he is available and able to compete," he said. "No sanction is going to bring [De Miguel] back to us."

articles.title: Statue to honor Gaudreau brothers at South Jersey rink
articles.summary: A life-size bronze statue of John and Matty Gaudreau will be installed at their childhood rink in South Jersey.
articles.body:
A life-size statue honoring John and Matty Gaudreau is planned for the South Jersey rink where the brothers learned to play hockey.

The bronze artwork, created by South Jersey sculptor Carl LeVotch, will stand outside the Hollydell Ice Arena in Sewell, the project's organizers said in a statement.

LeVotch, known for his sports-themed creations, plans to begin 3-D sketches in clay and wax by December. He will then produce a 17-inch model for casting with the finished sculpture due by Spring 2028, the statement said.

The completed work and its base are expected to weigh approximately 1,000 pounds.

The sculpture has the endorsement of Guy and Jane Gaudreau, the parents of John and Matty.

The Hollydell Drive rink is where the brothers learned to play hockey "and it will always hold a special place in our hearts as a family," they said in the statement.

"We hope every young player who walks through those doors sees it and is inspired to play the way John and Matty did, with heart and love for the game, and to live the way they did, with kindness on and off the ice," the parents said.

The brothers — Johnny, 31, and Matt, 29 — died Aug. 29, 2024, when a driver hit them as they bicycled on the narrow shoulder of a rural road in their native Salem County.

The elder brother, popularly known as "Johnny Hockey," was an all-star for the NHL's Columbus Blue Jackets. Matthew Gaudreau had also played professionally and coached the sport.

The motorist who allegedly struck them, 45-year-old Sean Higgins of Pilesgrove, is awaiting trial on charges that include two counts of reckless vehicular homicide while driving drunk. Jury selection is to begin on Dec. 1.

LeVotch said the planned Gaudreau Brothers Inspiration Sculpture will invite young athletes "to understand that character, compassion, and community are measures of greatness."

His public works include statues of boxing champions Joe Walcott in Camden and Joey Giardello in Philadelphia.

A New Jersey-based nonprofit, the Gaudreau Brothers Sculpture Project, has created a website to accept donations for the project.

articles.title: Vinicius hits 12-minute hat-trick as Brazil thrash Singapore
articles.summary: Vinicius Junior hit a 12-minute hat-trick in the first half as Brazil turned on the style in a 7-0 trouncing of Singapore on Tuesday.Vinicius was denied by I...
articles.body:
Vinicius Junior hit a 12-minute hat-trick in the first half as Brazil turned on the style in a 7-0 trouncing of Singapore on Tuesday.

Endrick, Estevao, Rayan and substitute Allan also scored as the South Americans brushed aside the hosts with a dominant performance at the National Stadium.

Brazil were much changed from their 3-2 loss to Japan on Saturday in which manager Carlo Ancelotti and captain Raphinha were shown red cards, with Vinicius one of only four players retaining their places in the starting line-up.

Bruno Guimaraes took over as skipper and set up the opener after nine minutes, playing a quick pass to Vinicius who wrong-footed Singapore captain Hariss Harun with his first touch before despatching a left-footed shot past goalkeeper Izwan Mahbud.

The Real Madrid forward notched his second in the 15th minute after a quick counter-attack as Endrick laid the ball off for his unmarked team-mate to slot home.

Vinicius was denied by Izwan shortly afterwards but he completed his hat-trick in the 21st minute when he was found unmarked in the six-yard box by Estevao's low centre.

Rayan had an effort disallowed for offside but Endrick added to Brazil's lead in the 31st minute with a low effort from range which found the bottom right corner.

Estevao also had a goal disallowed for a foul by Vinicius but the Chelsea winger added to Brazil's tally just after the interval with a deflected shot from the edge of the box.

Rayan rocked the crossbar soon after but the endeavour of the Bournemouth forward was rewarded in the 65th minute when he rounded substitute goalkeeper Syazwan Buhari to make it 6-0.

Brazil rang the changes in the closing stages and Allan came off the bench to grab the seventh goal in the 74th minute.

Speaking in the absence of the suspended Ancelotti, Brazil assistant Francesco Mauri lauded the commitment shown by Vinicius.

"His attitude was fantastic. As we discussed before the match, you shouldn't focus solely on the quality of the opponents, you just have to give your absolute best," said the Italian.

"He was a constant threat, providing great depth to our attack. He forced the opposition to double-mark him, which in turn allowed us to defend a bit more effectively."

Despite lengthy travel for the friendlies in Singapore, Mauri felt the effort had been worthwhile for the squad's development.

"Before the game, we told the players that it was really important to finish in the best way in these November FIFA dates because after this we have to wait until March for our next games, so it's good to go home with a good feeling," he said.

articles.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo dismisses emotional Bucks reunion with cold six word response
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Bucks will face a familiar opponent on Wednesday night when Giannis Antetokounmpo takes the court for the Miami Heat for the first time since l...
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Bucks will face a familiar opponent on Wednesday night when Giannis Antetokounmpo takes the court for the Miami Heat for the first time since leaving Milwaukee after 13 seasons. Antetokounmpo and his new team are riding a five-game winning streak after beating the Houston Rockets 128-110, giving Miami eight victories in its last 10 games. The two-time MVP also addressed whether facing his former team would bring any special emotions.

Few players have shaped the Bucks' history like Antetokounmpo , who helped bring Milwaukee its first NBA title in half a century back in 2021. His departure came through a trade to Miami that also involved Bobby Portis Jr. Despite spending 13 seasons with the franchise, the 31-year-old is downplaying the reunion, saying he views Wednesday's matchup as "just another game."

"It's gonna be just another game," commented the Greek Freak.

"I'm gonna do the same thing, I'm gonna eat the same meal, I'm gonna kiss my kids before they go to bed. Get ready, wake up, do my routine. Get ready for the game, same game, same thing. It doesn't change. It doesn't matter the jersey."

Giannis Antetokounmpo's first match against the Milwaukee Bucks

Antetokounmpo discussed the upcoming reunion after putting together 20 points on 8-of-11 shooting, converting four of six free throws, and adding 13 rebounds and six assists against Houston. His latest performance helped Miami secure another victory, while the Heat also made a defensive statement by limiting a top Western Conference opponent to 41.3% shooting overall and 27.8% from three-point range. With the win behind them, attention now turns to Wednesday's matchup against Milwaukee.

Although Wednesday's matchup will take place in Miami, Antetokounmpo was asked whether a return to Milwaukee would carry greater emotional weight . The former Bucks star once again played down the significance, maintaining that he does not view the reunion as anything more than a regular game.

"I haven't found myself being emotional; I think the only time I've been emotional was when we won the championship," remarked the former Bucks star.

"Played my whole career, I haven't found myself putting emotion into the game. I feel like emotions are for movies, and this is just basketball. Just I'm gonna do prep, get my body ready, and get ready for the game."
