articles.title: 'I've heard': What Bam Adebayo has done behind the scenes to 'make it work' with Giannis Antetokounmpo
articles.summary: The Miami Heat are looking like a more complete team again after their terrible start to the season. The Heat lost each of their first four games of the camp...
articles.body:
The Miami Heat are looking like a more complete team again after their terrible start to the season.

The Heat lost each of their first four games of the campaign and were viewed by many as the worst team in the division at that stage. Since then, they have won eight of their 10 games and are now looking brilliant.

Giannis Antetokounmpo has been consistently brilliant, but the one player who has recently stepped up is Bam Adebayo.

Bam Adebayo sought help to 'make it work' with Giannis Antetokounmpo

Adebayo had his struggles early on in the season.

Everyone knows how good a player the 29-year-old can be, but there were times when he just didn't look like his usual aggressive self.

That led to a lot of criticism, with people like Michael Beasley claiming that Adebayo looks like he doesn't even want to be there anymore.

However, in the recent games against the Pistons and the Cavaliers, Adebayo came up with a combined 57 points, 19 rebounds and seven assists.

His partnership with Antetokounmpo looks a lot better now, and Marc J. Spears has revealed one of the reasons why.

Adebayo apparently reached out to people behind the scenes to figure out how to play with the Greek superstar and succeed alongside him.

Spears said on ESPN: "Bam and Klay were both saying, 'This is a work in progress. Be patient.'

"I've heard that Bam has kind of reached out to people, trying to figure out ways, showing some leadership and trying to work with Giannis.

"Remember the Heatles were like 10-8 – they started off this way, this is the new Heatles, you could say. They are a work in progress, and it's going great now.

"They are 7-2 off late, they are winning, and these guys are figuring it out. And I think they're going to get better and better and better.

"So, shoutout to Bam for trying to figure out a way to make it work."

Adebayo was in action for the Heat in their most recent game against the Houston Rockets. He played 16 minutes, scored four points and recorded one rebound, two assists and two steals.

However, a right hip problem ruled him out of the rest of the game, which was a real shame, just as he was starting to look like his usual self again.

Thankfully, though, coach Erik Spoelstra revealed after the game that he does not expect Adebayo to be sidelined long-term.

articles.title: Jumbo Package: Alabama’s Special Teams deserve a shout out
articles.summary: First up today, we have Ryan Grubb’s press conference: “Direct snap to Ryan. Should have been outside zone blocking. [Right tackle] Jayvin [James] and I thin...
articles.body:
First up today, we have Ryan Grubb's press conference:

"Direct snap to Ryan. Should have been outside zone blocking. [Right tackle] Jayvin [James] and I think it was Michael [Carroll] at guard should still have zoned up," Grubb said on Monday. "They double-teamed, left the defensive end. [Tight end] Kaleb [Edwards] was supposed to block the overhang. The fake reverse leaves the corner for Ryan, and that was it. "We didn't do that. We blocked duo. Yeah, we just didn't execute in that moment. It sucked. Looked stupid. Could have crammed it in there for a yard, certainly. Yeah, I was pissed off. It was bad. I was looking for a big hit there to Ryan, and I don't think there was any prayer that kid tackles him out on the perimeter."

"Direct snap to Ryan. Should have been outside zone blocking. [Right tackle] Jayvin [James] and I think it was Michael [Carroll] at guard should still have zoned up," Grubb said on Monday. "They double-teamed, left the defensive end. [Tight end] Kaleb [Edwards] was supposed to block the overhang. The fake reverse leaves the corner for Ryan, and that was it.

"We didn't do that. We blocked duo. Yeah, we just didn't execute in that moment. It sucked. Looked stupid. Could have crammed it in there for a yard, certainly. Yeah, I was pissed off. It was bad. I was looking for a big hit there to Ryan, and I don't think there was any prayer that kid tackles him out on the perimeter."

I couldn't find a good article transcribing his entire press conference this time, but Grubb has quite a few soundbites in his opening diatribe, and the reporters asked some good questions this time too. People are always going to be angry at Grubb blaming players, but I don't mind this answer for two reasons – 1) it's a legitimate breakdown of what went wrong, and 2) his comment "I was looking for a big hit there to Ryan" was telling. Grubb wasn't going for a 3rd down conversion, he was going for the home run. Do I agree with it? No, not really. But at least I know why.

Grubb also specifically pointed out Danny Lewis as being a guy who played great, and I wanted to emphasize that. I thought Lewis did an excellent job, especially at getting yards after his couple of catches. He's been known as a blocker his whole career and has struggled with health the entire time, so it's good to see him getting his chance in the passing game.

With all the angst centering around Grubb and the offense, it seems no one felt like writing anything about what he said.

I noticed in his opening remarks that he specified they looked at "62 different run looks" in preparation for the Vanderbilt game. You don't say something that specific without it being something that's been on your mind, so it's clear that Vanderbilt is still an opponent that has been locking in Wommack's brain. And it's shown – they've held the Commodores to their season low in scoring the last two years in a row.

There are always going to be new problems to correct, but I like that Wommack has a relentless drive to fix things that do go wrong and try to not let them come back.

"I think good offense, defense. I think one thing to continue to highlight that I'm proud of also is just the special teams, and the two returns in particular. The big one with Dijon, the Ryan-Coleman Williams punt return. It wasn't the effect and the impact that Dijon's was, but a lot of good individual efforts that are being made. Smart decisions, because a lot of penalties can happen in those moments, a lot of space to cover. And just the execution, you can see a lot of — there's still a few first-year players out there and a lot of second-year guys and even some third-year guys that are out there executing in those moments. I think our coverage units continue to be consistent. A lot of the kicks go through the back of the end zone. But we squib kick and we got Lotzeir Brooks rolling. A lot of times, you would never expect him to be the first guy to make that play, and he's hunting guys down. And so, punt team coverage, I think, continues to be done at a high level because of effort, and as long as we have that, we'll continue to have that success."

Quietly, the Alabama special teams has made major improvements this year, and I think it's made a big difference in their success as a team thus far.

Last year? Alabama averaged 38.6 net yards per punt, while they averaged 17.1 and 8.0 in kick and punt returns.

This year? 43.3 net yards per punt with 29.2 and 9.9 yards per return on kicks and punts. Oh, and 12/14 on field goals instead of 16/23.

If you're the advanced metrics type, Alabama was ranked 111th in the country in FPI special teams efficiency, and #103 in SP+ . But this year, they're ranked 29th in FPI and 14th in SP+

Just good stuff, and for all the vitriol we gave special teams coach Jay Nunez after last season, I'll give him credit where it's due this this season for the massive turnaround.

articles.title: Ravens in 'do or die' mode after loss to 0-8 Chargers
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens are now in "do or die" mode after a brutal loss to the 0-8 Los Angeles Chargers, safety Kyle Hamilton told reporters.
articles.body:
Nov. 17 (UPI) -- The Baltimore Ravens are now in "do or die" mode after a brutal loss to the 0-8 Los Angeles Chargers, safety Kyle Hamilton told reporters.

Hamilton's Ravens dropped to 4-6 as a result of the 23-20 setback Monday in Baltimore. The Ravens, who went 4-1 to start the season, head into a two-game road trip with a five-game losing streak.

"This week, we just have to have an outlook of, 'look, it's do or die at this point,'" Hamilton said. "You show what you're made of, and we're going to rock with who we're going to rock with."

The Ravens held advantages of 347 to 287 in total yards, 22-15 in first downs and 41.7% to 15.4% in third-down conversions. But they also were out-gained 160 to 16 on the ground and lost the turnover battle 2-0.

The 16 rushing yards for the Ravens, the AFC's third-best rushing attack, were their fewest since 2016.

"At the end of the day, it's an individual thing," Hamilton said. "As a team, we've got to come together, but you've got to look yourself in the mirror and say 'what do you want out of this?' Do you just want to get through the year and be a whatever team?

"That's fine, but you shouldn't be here."

The Ravens, who are playing without injured star quarterback Lamar Jackson, sit in last place in the AFC North. They are now 0-4 at home and 2-5 against teams in the AFC, including 0-2 against divisional foes. They are ninth in the conference standings.

Hamilton noted that the Ravens started 1-5 last season, but went on a five game-winning streak to jump back into contention. They proceeded to go 2-4 over the final six weeks of the season.

The All-Pro safety, who leads the No. 4 defense in the AFC, called on fellow Ravens leaders to step up.

"It's up to us leaders to kind of uphold a standard," Hamilton said. "The standard has been what it is around here since '96. Right now, we are disgracing the standard as players, as a team.

Veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who made his first start since being traded to the Ravens on Nov. 6, completed 33 of 49 passes for 340 yards and an interception in Monday's loss. The Chargers held star running back Derrick Henry to just 10 yards off 10 carries. That yardage total was the second-lowest of his career for a game in which he received at least 10 carries.

"Heck of a run wall, big emphasis on that,'' Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said. "I thought that was really good. Linebackers played extremely well. Edges were putting the pressure on too. Just trying not to let [Henry] get started. Guys just battled the whole night.''

Meanwhile, Chargers running back Omarion Hampton ran for a season-high 105 yards, the second-best total of his career.

Despite a slow start and offensive turbulence, the Ravens remained in striking distance late in the Week 10 clash. They trailed just 23-20 with 2:03 remaining when a fumble from wide receiver Zay Flowers at the Chargers' 46-yard line killed momentum. Brissett also launched a pass toward the end zone in the final seconds, but that ball was knocked down at the Chargers' 4-yard line.

"It's a frustrating loss," Brissett said. "One that we thought we should have had. It's a tough way for this game to go. But also saw the look in the guys' eyes in that room and the urge to want to get it right."

Henry, who totaled 3,516 rushing yards and averaged 5.6 yards per carry from 2024 through 2025, logged just 3.8 yards per attempt through his first 10 starts this season.

"I'm never not going to believe that we can't turn it around and play the way we want to play," Henry said. "You go through tough stretches, but you still gotta go to work. The season's still going to be here."

Henry and the Ravens will take on the Carolina Panthers (4-5) at 1 p.m. EST Sunday in Charlotte, N.C. The Chargers (1-8) will host the New York Jets (2-8) at 4:05 p.m. Sunday in Inglewood, Calif.

articles.title: Bethell to have more surgery and out of SA tour
articles.summary: Jacob Bethell will miss England’s Test tour of South Africa because he requires more surgery on the knee injury that has kept him out since July.
articles.body:
Jacob Bethell will miss England's Test tour of South Africa because he requires more surgery on the knee injury that has kept him out since July.

Batter Bethell was due to make his return in the ongoing white-ball tour of Australia, but had to leave that trip at the weekend after suffering what England described as a "setback" in training.

The 23-year-old has met with a specialist and, as first reported by the Telegraph, will have a second operation on his right knee.

England are yet to confirm Bethell's replacement for the three Tests in South Africa.

When the Warwickshire man missed the three Tests against Pakistan during the home summer, his place in the England squad went to Ollie Pope.

Bethell has not played since the third one-day international against India at Lord's in July, when he suffered discomfort in his knee.

In his absence from the Test side during the Pakistan series, Emilio Gay opened and Jordan Cox took Bethell's slot at number three.

It was expected that one of Gay or Cox would have to drop out of the starting XI in South Africa to make way for Bethell's return.

When England announced their touring squad last week, selector Marcus North said that no decisions had been made on the make-up of the first-choice top six.

Now, in Bethell's continued absence, Gay and Cox will have further opportunities to make claims for a long-term place in the Test side.

Surrey's Pope has not played for England since the third Ashes Test against Australia in Adelaide in December of last year.

He was due to be with the Lions in South Africa on a tour that overlaps with the Test series and appears the most likely candidate to replace Bethell.

If England opt against Pope, Somerset's James Rew and uncapped Durham opener Ben McKinney have both been in strong form on the Lions' recent white-ball tour of the West Indies.

This latest setback is a significant blow to Bethell, who looked to have cemented his place in the Test side with a sparkling century in the final Ashes Test in Sydney in January.

But the knee injury cut short his summer, meaning he missed The Hundred, the Pakistan series, white-ball matches against Sri Lanka, then the limited-overs tours of Pakistan and Australia.

The second surgery would also leave him as a doubt for England's other winter Tests: two in Bangladesh in February and the one-off 150th anniversary day-nighter against Australia in Melbourne in March.

England are already without Josh Tongue for the first Test against South Africa in Johannesburg, beginning on 17 December. The pace bowler will be at home for the birth of his second child.

North has previously confirmed that England will call on fast-bowling reserves from the Lions to cover for Tongue.

articles.title: Stavros Halkias hilariously reacts to Ravens blunder on 'Manningcast'
articles.summary: The Baltimore native had a rough night
articles.body:
A once promising season has turned into a complete disaster for the Baltimore Ravens . Their latest nationally televised heartbreak came Monday night against the Los Angeles Chargers, as Jim Harbaugh's team won its first game of the season to spoil Jacoby Brissett's Baltimore debut.

Ravens fans are growing increasingly frustrated, even among the celebrity ranks. Baltimore native and comedian Stavros Halkias appeared on the Manningcast last night, and he had the unfortunate opportunity to watch Zay Flowers' backbreaking fourth-quarter fumble alongside Peyton and Eli.

Halkias' reaction was as animated as you'd expect.

"Brutal," Halkias said . "I can't believe I agreed to do this (expletive) . This (expletive) sucks."

Halkias speaks for all Ravens fans on that one. Jesse Minter's squad has lost five consecutive games after a 4-1 start, and with Lamar Jackson nowhere close to returning, this season is quickly becoming a wrap.

articles.title: The Season That Was: Trey Yesavage
articles.summary: Trey Yesavage was the Blue Jays’ first-round draft pick in 2024. He made it to the Jays in September 2025, made three starts, then made five starts and a rel...
articles.body:
Trey Yesavage was the Blue Jays' first-round draft pick in 2024. He made it to the Jays in September 2025, made three starts, then made five starts and a relief appearance in our playoff run with a 3.58 ERA. In 27.2 innings, he allowed 18 hits, 11 walks, and had 39 strikeouts. The Jays were hoping that teams would have problems with his 'over the top' delivery. His pitches come off his hand at 7.1 feet off the ground (decimal points in imperial measurements look so weird to me), and it seemed they did.

We wondered how he would do in a full season. Unfortunately, we didn't find out as he missed a fair bit of time with an injury.

Provided by Baseball-Reference.com : View Original Table Generated 11/16/2026.

Baseball Reference has him at 2.0 WAR, and Fangraphs has him at 1.3, valuing him at $10.0 million to the Blue Jays.

Trey had a 4.22 FIP and 4.57 xFIP which explains why his fWAR is lower than his bWAR

He had a .214 BABIP (team average .283). 74.8% of the base runners he allowed were stranded (team average 72.4).

Yesavage's line drive rate was 16.4% (team average 19.4). His ground ball rate was 32.2% (team 42.3). And the fly ball rate was 50.4% (team 38.2). 8.1% of his fly balls left the park 9.5% of the time (team 11.0).

His strikeout rate was 24.2% (team 23.1), while his walk rate was up 11.7% (team 9.7).

Trey's soft contact rate was 16.1% (team 17.2). Hard contact was 31.8% (team 32.3).

He was slightly better vs. RHB (..174/.263/.356) than LHB (.195/.300/.349).

Yesavage was better on the road (batters hit.172/.281/.316 with a 3.20 ERA) than at home (.200/.287/.388 with a 4.21 ERA).

He was about the same in the first half (3.72, .182/.288/.333) as the second half (3.57, .200/.270/.413), but he only pitched 22.2 innings in the second half.

April: 1 start, 1-0, 0.00. Batters hit .200/.200/.250 with 0 home runs, 0 walks and 3 strikeouts.

May: 6 starts, 1-2, 2.56. Batters hit .202/.313/.284 with 0 home runs, 17 walks and 36 strikeouts.

June: 5 starts, 2-1, 4.75. Batters hit .165/.258/.404 with 6 home runs, 13 walks and 22 strikeouts..

July: 5 starts, 1-2, 4.81. Batters hit .198/.308/.372 with 2 home runs, 15 walks and 0 strikeouts.

August: 1 start (just 2 innings), 0-0, 0.00. Batters hit .000/.143/.000 with 0 home runs, 1 walk and 30 strikeouts.

September: 2 starts (4 innings), 0-1, 4.50. Batters hit .214/.267/.643 with 2 home run, 1 walks and 6 strikeouts.

The Jays were 7-13 in his starts. They averaged 3.63 runs per game in his starts. They scored 3 or fewer runs in 13 of his starts.

4 days, 8 starts: 3-3, 2.85 ERA, batters hit .188/.276/.333.

5 days, 6 starts: 0-2, 4.23 ERA, batters hit .172/.289/.343.

6 or more days: 4 starts, 2-1, 4.42 ERA, batters hit .212/.289/.409.

Tyler Heineman: 3 games, 14.1 innings: 1.26 ERA, batters hit .220/.350/.260.

Alejandro Kirk: 9 games, 35 innings: 4.63 ERA, batters hit .171/.309/.358.

Brandon Valenzuela: 8 games, 48.1 innings: 3.72 ERA, batters hit .187/.242/.374.

Trey was good with RISP, holding batters to a .149/.269/.216 line.

In high-leverage spots, batters hit .241/.343/.407. Low leverage .167/.254/.333.

His best start, according to GameScore, was a 76 on May 20th, at Yankee Stadium. He went 6 innings, allowing 2 hit, 0 walks, and 8 strikeouts.

The worst start was a 31 GameScore. July 7th, going 1.2 innings, allowing 1 hits, 4 earned run, 7 walks and 1 strikeouts in San Diego. 5 outs and 7 walks.

It wasn't the season we hoped for from Trey, mostly because of injuries. He had a shoulder issue at the start of the season and then missed time after 'meniscus surgery' in early August, throwing just four innings after that, near the end of the season. But it does look like we'll enjoy watching him when he can put together an injury-free season.

I said, before the season, that his 'over the top' delivery does worry me. Sometimes, when you have a delivery so different from anyone else's, we find out why no one else throws that way. But one season isn't enough of a sample size to prove anything.

The team was careful with him during spring training and, well, it didn't pay off. Not that being careful was what caused his injury troubles. It more showed they were right to be careful. He's still just 23 (24 at the end of July); he has plenty of time to become the top-of-the-rotation starter we were hoping he'd be.

If the over/under on Trey's innings was 150 I'd take the….24.2% of us were pessimistic and right.

If the over.under on Trey's ERA is 3.50 I'd take the…..44.4% of us were pessimistic and right again.

And we asked if Trey would win a Cy Young in his career. 40% of us said yes and I'm still hopeful.

articles.title: Adebayo’s Absence Shifts Heat-Bucks Focus To Herro Rivalry
articles.summary: With Bam Adebayo sidelined by hip tightness, the Heat-Bucks matchup loses its star clash. Tyler Herro now faces the spotlight alone against Milwaukee.
articles.body:
The long-awaited Bam Adebayo versus Tyler Herro showdown likely won't happen as planned on Wednesday night. Adebayo sat out the second half of Monday's game against the Houston Rockets due to right hip tightness. Now, his availability for the Milwaukee Bucks game remains uncertain. The Heat will have to find another way to handle their former teammate and the Bucks' new center. Giannis Antetokounmpo will likely start at the five spot if Adebayo cannot go.

Heat fans have waited all summer to see how these two former teammates interact on the court. Instead, the narrative shifts to how Miami survives without its defensive anchor. Adebayo played just 15 minutes and 31 seconds before leaving the floor on Monday. He finished with four points and one rebound in that short stint. The team has not set a return date, leaving the frontcourt rotation in flux. This injury interrupts a promising run where the Heat won seven of their last nine games. The plan to build chemistry between Adebayo and Antetokounmpo faces a sudden test.

Without Adebayo, the Heat lose their primary rim protector and versatile defender. Coach Erik Spoelstra already moved Antetokounmpo to center and inserted Andrew Wiggins into the starting lineup. This change gives the team more perimeter speed but less size in the paint. The Bucks, led by Antetokounmpo, will now face a smaller defensive front. Miami needs Wiggins to make shots while the big man handles the paint. Wiggins made three of six 3-point attempts during the second half of Monday's game. The team must adjust quickly to avoid losing the lead they held before Adebayo left.

Tyler Herro has been criticized for burning bridges during his exit, but his talent remains undeniable. Ira Winderman of the Sun Sentinel noted that Herro deserves recognition as one of the Heat's all-time best players. The question of whether he can score against his old team is secondary to the Heat's injury crisis. Miami cannot rely on a single matchup to win a game. The team needs a collective effort to cover the gap left by Adebayo's absence. Davion Mitchell has been a key part of the recent success, leading the team in assists with 9.2 per game. Klay Thompson also brings veteran experience, having made 53 three-pointers this season.

The Heat will assess Adebayo's hip condition before Wednesday night. If he cannot go, the burden falls on the remaining stars to step up. Antetokounmpo leads the team in points with 28.3 and rebounds with 12.5 per game. In eight of his 14 games with Miami, he has scored at least 30 points. The team hopes to keep building momentum despite this setback. "We have to keep building," Adebayo said in a recent interview with Fox Sports Radio. The Heat face a tough test against a Bucks team looking to exploit any weakness. The final decision on Adebayo's status will be made before the game on Wednesday.

articles.title: NHL Predictions: Ottawa Senators vs Winnipeg Jets – November 17
articles.summary: In today's NHL Predictions, the Ottawa Senators hit the road to the geographic centre of Canada to take on the Winnipeg Jets, presented by us, fine folks her...
articles.body:
In today's NHL Predictions , the Ottawa Senators hit the road to the geographic centre of Canada to take on the Winnipeg Jets, presented by us, fine folks here at Last Word On Hockey . This is a Jets team on the upswing against a Sens team that, let's be honest, has been rolling to start 2026-27 at 13-6-2, good for a three-way tie for the top of the Atlantic Division. So, let's get to it, time to get sensational.

Head-to-Head History and Game Details for Jets vs Senators

Tonight's game is a special one for a hockey family and the Ottawa Senators organization, as their first selection, tenth overall from the 2021 NHL Entry Draft , and son of former NHL goalie Brian Boucher , tough guy Tyler Boucher, will make his long-anticipated NHL debut versus the Winnipeg Jets.

Boucher has been given every opportunity to succeed. He is skilled and brings toughness. It remains to be seen if he can develop into a late bloomer. He has five goals and five assists in 17 games for the AHL's Belleville Senators to begin 2026-27. Additionally, one neat fact about the hockey lineage of this meeting is that the Sens veteran leader, Claude Giroux , was a Philadelphia Flyer when Brian played his final NHL game in March of 2013. Cool.

Tonight's game will be an early start at 7:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time for a Winnipeg Jets home game, live from the Canada Life Centre in Winnipeg, Manitoba.

US TV: ESPN+ || Canada TV: RDS2, TSN3 (Jets Region), TSN5 (Senators Region), Sportsnet+, and available wherever you are on the NHL Center Ice Package.

Looking at some numbers, the Sens continue to struggle on the power play, at 11.5 percent success rate, they sit 32nd. Winnipeg is much more reasonable at 24.2 percent, good for 12th league wide. The two teams score at about the same rate overall, which is impressive for Ottawa, considering their lacklustre power play. Ottawa scores 3.14 goals-per-game, while Winnipeg is 3.10.

Ottawa has had its share of adversity this year, with injuries, and now more recently rumours popping up. They just need to focus on playing their game, and hoping their secondary scoring continues to provide just enough to get them these victories early on in the campaign.

The guy that has been hot, was the birthday boy two games ago now, Shane Pinto. Moreover, he even scored the overtime winner versus the Colorado Avalanche , although he was kept off the scoreboard versus the Pittsburgh Penguins. Still, his last five games has seen him average over 21 minutes a game, and lead the Sens with four goals and six points.

On the injury front for the Senators, Andre Burakovsky skated yesterday, but Warren Foegele has not hit the ice, as of yet. But it was encouraging that head coach Travis Green did suggest that the Nick Cousins injury won't keep him out long. He had taken a hard hit from Washington's Jakob Chychrun, but does seem to recovering well. That is great news.

Winnipeg can be tough to play, and we suggest not letting Mark Scheifele get to the net, especially on those power play opportunities. Adam Lowry, these are guys that take the puck to the net, and don't get denied. What makes Winnipeg so tricky is that they mix in speed and skill with Kyle Connor or Cole Perfetti to cross up defences…but not the Sens. Sens will have to use their strength of strong defensive zone positioning to cut off the Jets, and take puck possession.

We can't talk about Winnipeg's story without talking about the heater that Scheifele is on. Scheifele is riding a six-game point streak, with four goals and nine assists. It has him up to 19 assists and 26 total points in 21 games on the campaign. Furthermore, Scheifele just recently became the Jets all-time leader in points, now sitting four ahead of Dale Hawerchuk with 933 in 982 career regular season games played. Also, Kyle Connor is moving up the list and is fifth with 700 in just 716 games.

Winnipeg is a bit banged up, including Dylan DeMelo , Kyle Connor, Nick Bjugstad, Vlaidslav Namestnikov, and Elias Salomonsson .

Connor was just listed as day-to-day, so very well might play. Salomonsson might return, as he was away on personal leave, and was back practicing with the club yesterday. Meanwhile, one-time Sen Dylan DeMelo took a crunch and went down awkwardly against Mikko Rantanen. He is listed as week-to-week.

Winnipeg will look for the advantage through the special teams. If they can shut Ottawa down five-on-five, it will be a tough one for Ottawa to win.

Sen fans don't need to be reminder that Linus Ullmark is red hot, and people are not out of place to say he would very likely win the Vezina Trophy if it were handed out in mid-November. His dazzling .939 save percentage and 1.47 goals-against average lead all NHL netminders, as you might well expect.

But we are here for interesting facts, because we are cool like that. In Ottawa Senator franchise history, Ullmark has now joined only Martin Gerber to start an NHL season with nine wins in their first 10 games.

Winnipeg's starter should be their number one, and Stuart Skinner. His first year as a Jets is going all right, given the unknown expectations coming into the year. But they had assets, and they are hoping in the future, it will be a difference maker.

The Senators have been playing so well thus far, we do see them coming away with the two points. They will look to capitalize on the goaltending matchup, and the depth throughout their lineup.
